Following up with internal suggested pricing notes for Acme based on their 250M baseline. Quick model: 

- Benchmarking (approx): OpenAI (large chat-capable model) ~$40	360 per 1M tokens; Anthropic ~$35	350 per 1M tokens (public host pricing for comparable performance).
- Open-model hosts (quantized/dedicated infra) can get to ~$10	325 per 1M tokens depending on compression/throughput and whether we use dedicated capacity.

Proposed Redwood offer (preferential for committed volumes):
- Committed (monthly reserved pool, 250M/month): $19 per 1M tokens (maps to $4,750/month platform tokens cost) + monthly platform fee $1,500 (support, SLA, observability) => $6,250/month total effective (for 250M).
- On-demand (no commit): $27 per 1M tokens (higher to account for burst/dedicated capacity reservation risk).

Unit economics notes: at 250M tokens, model compute + infra + ops nets us a gross margin thats reasonable with the $19 committed price if we leverage batching, prefix cache, and a quantized 8-bit model variant.

Competitive angle vs OpenAI/Anthropic: we can highlight equivalent or better latency and observability, and a materially lower $/1M for comparable open-model variants. 

If you want, I drafted a short one-pager (attached to Marissa's outgoing) with the two rows (committed vs on-demand) and the spend mapping.

Appreciate the confirmation. I attached the one-pager with two commercial options (Committed vs On-demand) and a simple mapping to your 250M tokens/month. High-level summary from the one-pager: 

- Committed: $19 per 1M tokens => $4,750/month token spend + $1,500/month platform fee => $6,250/month total effective (for 250M/month). Committed includes a 6-month minimum and 99.9% availability SLA, SOC2 evidence, and a dedicated pool for consistent latency.
- On-demand: $27 per 1M tokens => $6,750/month token spend (no platform fee in the short quote) 1 higher unit to reflect burst risk.

Benchmarking context (for procurement):
- Public OpenAI large chat pricing (comparable capability): ~ $40	360 per 1M tokens for higher-tier models (noting these are public host prices and vary by model).
- Anthropic public tiers: ~ $35	350 per 1M tokens for comparable models.
- Typical open-model hosting (quantized, dedicated infra): ~ $10	325 per 1M depending on variant/commit and infra efficiency.

Why Redwood is competitive: dedicated pools + batching & prefix cache drive down your effective compute per token; our Dedicated/Private options let you pin a quantized model variant that preserves quality while reducing raw cost. We also include per-route observability and a simple rollback to public hosts if you want hybrid fallbacks.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Procurement: confirm they received the one-pager and SOC2 link (cc'd).
2) If they want committed pricing, confirm the 6-month term and start date 1 we can draft a simple contract and get a DocuSign prepared.
3) Tech: we'll schedule a short 30-minute runbook session to validate peak patterns and latency targets (Aditya will lead).
